subject: POC packaging: milestone-convertibility offer for Maya Systems
messages:
From: Anil Rao <anil.rao@mayasys.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: POC wrap-up — options for leftover runway

Karthik,

Thanks for running the POC with us — team saw strong accuracy for our NLU flows. We have about 9 days left on the time-boxed pilot and ~120k tokens remaining in the measured bucket. Before we extend time, procurement asked whether we can: 1) convert the unused runway into milestone-linked credits (so we only pay when a specific milestone completes), or 2) buy a fixed credit top-up.

They also asked if we can make a small commercial concession tied to a short commitment — they want a single invoice/amendment rather than monthly top-ups. High-level ask: convert remaining days into credits that trigger on two milestones (onboarding complete, pilot-to-prod cutover) and provide a discount on committed spend.

Can you send a written option set and the expected timelines for approvals? We need to brief procurement by Friday.

—Anil
Maya Systems | Head of Data Products
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anil Rao <anil.rao@mayasys.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC wrap-up — options for leftover runway

Anil — really glad to hear the POC hit the accuracy targets. Appreciate the clear asks. Below are three concrete options we typically propose for time-boxed pilots; I tailored them to the numbers you shared. I attached the POC usage report and a single‑page draft amendment to make procurement's life easier.

Options (summary):

1) Milestone-convert (preferred for both sides)
- We convert the unused runway (~120k tokens) into two milestone-triggered credit buckets: 60% on "onboarding complete" and 40% on "prod cutover".
- Commercial: Customer signs an amendment for a one-time commitment that converts to credits; if milestones are met within 60 days we apply a 12% discount to the converted value.
- Benefits: keeps spend aligned to outcomes and preserves runway transparency.

2) Top-up with single invoice (faster procurement)
- One-time top-up invoice for X tokens (you choose size).
- Commercial: standard volume discount tiers apply; for a top-up >= $15k we can offer 7% off list for this invoice.
- Benefits: quickest to approve; no milestone gating.

3) Extension + staged billing
- Extend the pilot for 14 days and roll over remaining tokens; payments billed at month-end.
- Commercial: no discount but gives extra time to validate.

Requests/next steps I need from you:
- Which option procurement prefers (1/2/3).
- If 1, confirm milestone definitions (I used onboarding complete = first production webhook processed; prod cutover = first 24h with >500 calls).
- Target signature date so I can provision the amendment and pricing matrix.

Procurement notes: Legal wants the amendment as a single DocuSign envelope (we've attached a draft). Finance needs PO number and billing contact to generate an invoice.

I copied Laura (Director, Sales) to signal that pricing is negotiable within reason — happy to work through quick counteroffers.

Attachments: POC-usage-report.csv, draft-amendment-MAYA.pdf

Thanks — I'll standby for which path you want and can fast-track the DocuSign envelope.

—Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Anil Rao <anil.rao@mayasys.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC wrap-up — options for leftover runway

Forwarding technical confirmation inline (quick note).

On 2026-10-03 11:02, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> Anil — really glad to hear the POC hit the accuracy targets.
> ...

Anil — quick technical notes to help you pick between the options:
- If you go milestone-convert, confirm whether the early cutover milestone will require sustained throughput (we saw spike tests to 200 qps during the POC). If yes, we recommend a short Dedicated pocket for the first 72 hours post-cutover (keeps latency consistent).
- The milestone buckets can be tokenized as credits that automatically consume from the converted balance; we can wire up alerts to show consumption per milestone.
- If procurement prefers a single invoice path, we can combine the top-up with an SLA addendum for the cutover weekend at no extra charge (to mitigate risk).

I'll prepare a one-page ops note for the amendment describing the throughput expectations and a recommended Dedicated burst window. That helps procurement and infra sign-off.

—Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Anil Rao <anil.rao@mayasys.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-06T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC wrap-up — options for leftover runway

Karthik / Monica / Laura — good set of options, thanks. Procurement reviewed the draft and prefers option 1 (Milestone-convert) but asked if Redwood will meet us halfway on the discount. Their ideal is 15% but they'll accept 12% with a quick single-amendment signature.

We can accept a 60/40 split across the two milestones as you proposed. Procurement will provide a PO once we have an executed DocuSign and a final invoice amount. Can you update the draft amendment to reflect a 12% discount and send the DocuSign link? If finance can net the invoice to our PO and show payment terms (Net 30), we can get this signed by Friday EOD.

Also please include the small ops note about a 72-hour Dedicated burst for cutover — they want that in writing as part of the amendment.

Thanks — will await the DocuSign.

—Anil
Head of Data Products, Maya Systems
